items.title: Stock composition and distinct analytical reagents
items.text: Cesium carbonate, oleic acid and ODE form a Cs-oleate stock that is stored under vacuum and reheated before use. A separate manganese chloride mixture contains dry ODE, oleic acid and technical oleylamine. Whole-stock charges remain distinct from the injected aliquots. The reported precursor-loading ratios are retained as source labels because final stock concentration and volume are not specified. Acidic ICP matrices and ionic calibration standards serve analytical roles, rather than synthesis inputs.

items.title: Five preparations and separately tested workups
items.text: The source reports five preparations: 150 and 200 °C at Mn/Cs 0.7, and 180 °C at 0.7, 0.5 and 0.35. These are not a crossed nine-condition grid or independently counted batches. Growth lasts 5 s before ice-water quenching. Primary isolation uses centrifugation without antisolvent, followed by vacuum drying and hexane redispersion. Hexane-only, isopropanol, ethyl acetate and methyl acetate trials retain their own outcomes; they are not combined into one purification recipe.

items.title: Reported phases and unresolved refinement details
items.text: The 150 °C product is assigned cubic CsMnCl3, while the 180 and 200 °C products are assigned rhombohedral CsMnCl3. Diffraction, SAED, microscopy and ICP provide distinct sample-specific observations. The original refinement tables retain zero occupancies, inconsistent Wyckoff labels, absent cell angles and missing 200 °C atomic coordinates without repair. Their availability does not by itself qualify a CIF, a measured nanocrystal geometry or an exact recipe–structure label.

items.title: Luminescence, aging and an unencapsulated device
items.text: The optimized 180 °C, Mn/Cs 0.5 sample reaches a reported 40% quantum yield, while the cubic sample is nonemissive. Steady spectra, decay fits, transient absorption and low-temperature film measurements retain separate specimen and acquisition contexts. Film phase stability differs from dispersion luminescence stability. The proof-of-concept device uses an unencapsulated NC film on glass, with dark, bare-glass and same-film aging comparisons; no polymer-encapsulation recipe or precise device efficiency is supplied.

items.title: Photocurrent proof-of-concept setup
items.text: A thin NC film is deposited on glass; its edge is placed directly on a silicon pn photodiode. Cover the surrounding diode area opaquely, place it in a dark box and illuminate perpendicular to the glass center using a lens-collimated warm-white-like beam. The experimental film is unencapsulated, not a demonstrated polymer-embedded recipe.

items.title: Measured optical distinction
items.text: Cubic NCs absorb at 275 nm and are nonemissive; rhombohedral NCs absorb around 280 nm and emit near 670 nm. The source reports 40% QY for the optimized sample,2.6 eV Stokes shift and 97 nm FWHM. Main and SI optical gaps are4.8 eV cubic and 5.0 eV rhombohedral. Table S4 separately prints282 nm for 0.35.

notes: C10: Delta/B=11.18 appears under the common wavenumber heading but is a dimensionless ratio by its expression. PLE peak labels/main rounded wavelengths differ slightly from exact table wavenumbers; retain separate literal and interpreted units.

C4: Figure 4c says Cs/Mn although methods and sample labels use Mn/Cs. S4a/c/d legends use1:3 and 1:4 whereas S4b uses0.5 and 0.35. Retain source-defined conditions and flag cross-legend association instead of equating inverted ratios.
C2: Main 5 upper size13.4±1.0 differs from Figure 3d13.4±0.9 and S3d13.4±0.8; main 7 gives 10.8–15.5 nm while the shown mean values top out13.4. Each source value retains its original scope.

C8: Printed tau_avg=sum Ai*taui with Ai percentages does not reproduce the table averages even when normalized by100. For 280 nm it gives 213.55239 µs, not240.12 µs. Preserve formula, coefficients and tabulated results without silently choosing another expression.
C13: Main 8 describes52 meV at 50K, but Figure S7 lowest visible marker is near 70K. No exact curve digitization or silent temperature correction.

items.title: Structural and photophysical interpretations
items.text: The authors connect phase, octahedral distortion and magnetic/electronic models to the different luminescence behavior. They discuss surface stabilization, d–d transitions, self-trapped excitons and possible defects, while leaving the exact microscopic mechanism unresolved. DFT bands, spectroscopic fits and cited bulk results remain distinct from directly measured nanocrystal properties. Source-equation inconsistencies and uncertain sample links are preserved.

items.title: Theory inputs and settings
items.text: Use primitive cell models based on reported cubic and rhombohedral structures; determine most stable magnetic state then bands. HSE06 and zero-order regular approximation treat scalar relativity. Γ-centered k meshes are 6×6×6 for cubic and 3×3×3 for rhombohedral. No computed state is a direct measured nanocrystal configuration.

items.title: Computed electronic structure
items.text: The cubic CB edge has dispersed Mn4s character, yielding indirect5.18 eV and direct5.37 eV gaps. The rhombohedral system is direct; Figure 5c marks Γ states at 5.35 and 5.37 eV. VB character includes Cl3p/Mn3d with dx2-y2 and dz2; model symmetry/spin restrictions are proposed to explain nonemissive cubic versus emissive rhombohedral behavior.

remaining_gaps: Dry ODE/OA/OlAm and anhydrous solvents are named without their full drying protocols; ODE/technical ligand isomer distributions and surface coverage are not measured.

Stock final volume/molarity, Ar/vacuum pressure, injection speed, stirring rpm, cooling trace, numerical overnight duration, primary redispersion amount and synthetic yield are absent. Source loading labels are retained without reconstructed molarity.

Five preparation labels are supported, but independent batch counts, exact aliquot sharing across measurements, deposition thicknesses and every stability/LSC sample loading label are not supplied. A common material family is not proof of the same specimen.
Alternative precipitation times, exact tested variant, fraction recovery, acid volumes and percentage basis are incomplete. Failed/no-visible-precipitation trials remain part of the source.

Printed coordinates, occupancies, B values and spacegroups are retained literally but require separate symmetry/geometry/scattering validation. No CIF, raw refinement or DFT input file is supplied in this local pair. Author interpretations of STEs, passivation and fitted parameters are not exact measured atomistic labels.

LSC film loading, thickness, preparation/drying detail, exact loading variant and device efficiency are absent. Protective polymer encapsulation and ligand engineering are proposed future work, not an observed current synthesis.
